### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **29** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/registry-question.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**26** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json babd5d4a2d252e452b469ea4ab5bc661ba3a0a84`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/registry-question.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **175** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json babd5d4a2d252e452b469ea4ab5bc661ba3a0a84` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a2f7e1dd5ef6b69f8b5a6d5805c5369e784c9682` — the merge of head `c29899531b0b5af7e168a876356ee8422baa815d` into base `babd5d4a2d252e452b469ea4ab5bc661ba3a0a84`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a2f7e1dd5ef6b69f8b5a6d5805c5369e784c9682 && git checkout a2f7e1dd5ef6b69f8b5a6d5805c5369e784c9682
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin babd5d4a2d252e452b469ea4ab5bc661ba3a0a84 c29899531b0b5af7e168a876356ee8422baa815d && git checkout -B drift-repro babd5d4a2d252e452b469ea4ab5bc661ba3a0a84 && git merge --no-ff c29899531b0b5af7e168a876356ee8422baa815d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json babd5d4a2d252e452b469ea4ab5bc661ba3a0a84
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs babd5d4a2d252e452b469ea4ab5bc661ba3a0a84` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

domain:server#5 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4cz4f7zEQZ2C9GTG382
Request: review (contract) · area E2b · head bb54e3a5 · Fixes #33593

Ruling A as amended (R1–R7): every record-currency follow layer is judged against its object as served (base + enabled extensions + the incoming layer in its slot). Declared `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, `!` title, minor changeset, new ADR-0087 semantic entry `record-currency-follow-extension-judged-as-served`.

Please judge in particular:
- `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save.ts` (+18) is outside the order's file list: a published `object_extension` single save now asks the follow door. Measured before the hunk: 200, bad amount served.
- `registry.ts` hunks outside the three follow-door call sites: `registerObject` records the contributor its slot replaces and `RegistrationRestorePoint` keeps the earliest per slot (R7 needs a "before" fold).
- R7 covers runs only. Single save and the batch writer still judge against the empty slot, so an unchanged own body re-saved over a pair a cold boot admitted is still refused, as on main. Proposed A (leave as is); the alternative B is in the PR's open question.
- Not measured locally: test:repo, objectql direct dependents, full dogfood battery, check:dual-build-cjs-loads / check:lean-entry-closure (no whole-repo build). The PR body's NOT MEASURED for check:dual-source-exports and check:entry-nameability is stale: both exit 0.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `fb22e7bd1bb99759f3b4998ce1d36206bf21de88`
Local-runs: none
Scope: `.changeset/33593-extension-follow-judged-as-served.md`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save.ts`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/registry-question.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/record-currency-aggregate-door.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/manifest-service-artifact-refusal-restores.test.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/protocol-batch-object-registration.test.ts`, `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.record-currency-follow-extension-judged-as-served.ts`

Read: the PR's own commits `4bc1aa0a`, `56474fc2`, `ccd83416`, `bb54e3a5`, `08fdd538`, `e61155be`, and the merge `fb22e7bd`. The merge brings in `origin/main` only. I checked that the PR's hunks in `registry.ts`, `record-currency-aggregate-door.ts` and `protocol-save.ts` are byte-identical before and after the merge (`git diff c32bb6cc bb54e3a5` against `git diff 605d7121 fb22e7bd`). I measured the ruling against the text of #33593 (ruling A, amended, R1–R7, and its Acceptance list). Line numbers below are at `fb22e7bd`. I ran no test, build or gate. Every behaviour below is by reading.

### ① Derived judgments

**R1–R6 match the ruling.**
- `recordCurrencyFollowRefusalOf` (`registry.ts:5866-5904`) builds the object as served with the layer in its slot (`servedFoldWithLayer`, `:5907-5924`) and hands that fold to the door. The door no longer has `partial` (`record-currency-aggregate-door.ts:536-547`), so an `extend` layer's following amounts and the other-ends loop are both asked (R1, R3, R4).
- No owner gives no fold, which gives no verdict (`registry.ts:5881`, R2).
- A disabled extension is withheld from the fold through `withholdDisabledExtensions` (R5).
- The other-ends sentence names the extension's package and field (`record-currency-aggregate-door.ts:600-616`, R6).
- Clause-② `yes (narrowing)` is correct. The PR also moves two answers the other way (refused to installed, R7). That is allowed under the narrowing arm, because narrowing is the dominant kind.

**Area point 1: the `protocol-save.ts` hunk (`:1257-1273`) is necessary, and it mirrors the batch writer, but it moves one answer more than it declares.**
- *Necessary.* Without it, a published single save of an `object_extension` never asks the follow door. The ruling's Acceptance names single save as one of the three faces. The PR body measured 200 and a served bad amount before the hunk.
- *Same shape as the batch writer.* It asks exactly what the batch writer already asks of an extension row (`batch-object-registration.ts:163-167`).
- *It reaches further than the follow door.* The call goes through `objectRegistrationRefusal(..., 'extend', { againstRegistry: true })` (`registry.ts:5738`). On a sealed registry that clears `bodyOnly`, so `judgeRegistrationDoors` also asks D6's summary door (`recordCurrencySummaryRefusal`, `registry.ts:5820`) of the extension body.

**must-fix M1: the `protocol-save.ts` hunk also asks D6's summary door of a published `object_extension` save. That moved answer is not declared anywhere.**
- *On `main`.* `objectExtensionItemRefusal` asks only `extendContributionRefusal` and the address checks. An extension that adds a `record` roll-up D6 refuses, or a record-mode amount that a registered parent rolls up, was stored and answered 200. Its write-through registration then failed with only a `console.warn` (`protocol-registry-hydration.ts:1515-1523`).
- *With this PR.* The same save is refused 422 and nothing is stored.
- *Not declared.* The changeset, the PR's Clause-② table and the new ADR-0087 entry do not mention it. `registry-question.ts:16-17` says the item "asks the follow door too", and says nothing of D6.
- *Fix, either one:*
  - (a) declare it. Add a FROM → TO line to the changeset and the PR table, extend the entry's `surface` and the `registry-question.ts` sentence to D6's roll-up half, and pin one D6-refused `object_extension` single save (422, nothing stored).
  - (b) narrow the hunk so it asks the follow door alone.
- I recommend (a): the batch writer already asks both doors of an extension row.

**Area point 2: the `registry.ts` hunks outside the three call sites are necessary and minimal.**
- R7 needs a "before" fold at run end. The run does not know what a slot held unless `registerObject` records it.
- The added code is small:
  - one local (`:6129`),
  - three assignments, one in each replacement arm (own `:6176`, overlay `:6193`, extend `:6200`),
  - one new field on `RunRegisteredObject`, passed at `:6227`,
  - `noteRegisteredObject` (`:3938-3942`) keeping the earliest `replaced` for a slot that is written twice. The nested-point merge at `:3962` goes through the same method, so the earliest is kept there too.
- I found nothing in these hunks that is not needed for R7.

**must-fix M2: R7's comparison keys on the full refusal message. That message includes the parent's list of code-field candidates, so a run that leaves the pair as it found it can still be refused.**
- *The key.* `followRefusalKey` (`record-currency-aggregate-door.ts:550-551`) is `objectName + fieldName + message`.
- *Why the message changes.* `recordCurrencyFollowedCodeError` ends with `codeFieldCandidates(parentFields)` (`packages/spec/src/data/record-currency-path.ts:88`, `:95`). That is the list of every ISO 4217 field on the parent.
- *Example.* A cold boot admits `suite_line.amount` following `invoice.title`. The parent's owner then upgrades and only adds an unrelated code field `cc`. The "before" reading says "it has none; declare one…". The "served" reading says "candidates: 'cc'". The keys differ, so the upgrade is refused over a pair it did not touch.
- *The texts claim otherwise.* The changeset (`:24`) says "A run is not refused over a pair it leaves as it found it". The entry (`:35-39`) says such a run "is now refused only when it changes the pair".
- *The wrong package is blamed again.* This is the same blame-the-innocent shape that #33593 fixes, now triggered by a widening of the parent.
- *Fix, either one:*
  - (a) key the comparison on the pair, not the prose: the object, the field, the followed pointer (or roll-up), and the refusal class. Pin the example above (installs).
  - (b) narrow the changeset and entry sentences to "a no-change upgrade".
- I recommend (a).

**must-fix M3: the R7 pins do not cover the `extend` arm.** R1 newly judges `extend` layers, so R7 must hold for an extension package's own no-change upgrade.
- The R7 pin (`manifest-service-artifact-refusal-restores.test.ts:929-939`) upgrades only the two owners (ledger and billing).
- Nothing upgrades `extender` unchanged over the amount the cold boot admitted.
- The line that makes that case pass is `replaced = contributors.splice(idx, 1)[0]` in the extend arm (`registry.ts:6200`). By reading, removing that capture would turn no pin red.
- *Add one pin.* `bootWith([... extender({ ext_amount: follows('invoice.title') })])`, then `manifest.register(extender({ ...same }, '1.0.1'))` installs.

**must-fix M4: the changeset puts the R7 line under all three askers, which is false for two of them, and it leaves one moved answer unlisted.**
- *The scope.* Changeset `:18` says the list below applies "at the end of an install / upgrade / reload run, in the batch writer, and on a published single save". The R7 bullet (`:24`) then says "FROM refused 422 TO installed".
- *Batch writer and single save.* Both judge against the empty slot (`registry.ts:5843`), so an own body re-saved unchanged is still refused there. The PR body says so, and the entry now says so (`:39`). The changeset, which ships as CHANGELOG, does not.
- *The unlisted moved answer.* Under R1 with an empty `before`, re-publishing an unchanged `object_extension` (single save, or a package-publish row in the batch writer) over an amount a cold boot admitted moves from admitted (on `main` the extension's following half was never asked) to refused 422. The first bullet says "adding an amount", which does not cover a re-publish.
- *Fix.* Scope the R7 bullet to runs, and add the re-publish line.

**Pins against R1–R7.**
- R1 (three shapes at run end, single save, batch writer), R2, R3 (both orders, at all three faces), R4, R5 (missing, disabled, same artifact) and R6 (removal, de-code, the sentence) are each pinned.
- R7 is pinned for both owners, and a CONTROL pins that an upgrade changing the pair is still refused.
- M3 is the gap. N2 below is a smaller one.
- The CONTROLs the ruling asked for are present: an own body, and parent plus extension in one install.

**ADR-0087 entry.** `18.record-currency-follow-extension-judged-as-served.ts` is well-formed: `id`, `surface`, `replacement`, `reason`, `acceptanceCriteria`, and no `conversionIds`, which is correct because there is no D2 conversion.
- It is discovered by directory, and the changeset carries exactly one marker, `registered record-currency-follow-extension-judged-as-served`.
- `Lint & Repo Gates`, which runs `check:adr-0087-registration`, was green at `bb54e3a5`. The merge did not touch this entry or the changeset marker.
- FROM/TO matches the code, except the two places named in M1 (D6 is missing from `surface`) and M2 (the "only when it changes the pair" sentence).

### ② Semver level

**minor ×3 is correct.**
- AGENTS.md (§ landing, item 3): a `Metadata-protocol` kind takes at least `minor` on every package the diff moves.
- The diff moves `@objectstack/objectql` (door and registry), `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` (save door) and `@objectstack/spec` (a new semantic entry). The changeset lists all three at `minor`.
- The title carries `!`.
- The BREAKING paragraph names who is affected: an `objectExtensions` entry or a stored `object_extension` item whose record-mode amount follows a bad parent field. It also names the fix: point at a field with `valueDomain: 'iso_4217_currency'`, or install the supplier first or in the same artifact.
- The paragraph's FROM/TO list needs M1 and M4.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Not Tier H, and not governed.**
  - The PR file list (8 files, +600/−86 from `gh api pulls/33621/files`) touches no row of `GOVERNED_SURFACES` (`scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs:1261-1273`): no `docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` or workflow path.
  - It is under the 3,000-changed-line threshold.
  - The `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` declaration makes it a contract review, not a Tier H landing. `Governed Surface Queue Guard` is green at `fb22e7bd`.
- `RecordCurrencyFollowRegistryView` loses `partial` and `extensionFieldsOf`. It is not exported from `packages/objectql/src/index.ts`, so the public API does not move.
- **Seat ruling needed: R7 on single save and the batch writer** (area point 3; the PR's open question). My review judgment is below. It is not a ruling.
  - *Why the text alone does not settle it.* R7's text says "upgrade", which in #33593 is a run. But R1 says "every layer", and the Acceptance asks for the Clause-② table "at run end, in the batch writer, and on single save".
  - *Why it matters now.* The batch writer serves "a package publish" (`registry.ts` `objectRegistrationRefusal` docblock). This PR makes that face, and single save, newly refuse an unchanged re-publish of an extension over an amount a cold boot admitted (M4).
  - *Not a reviewer's call.* Whether "upgrade" in R7 covers a package publish or a re-publish is the seat's to rule, not the reviewer's.
  - *My recommendation: A* (runs only, as built), for two reasons. The batch writer asks after its rows are registered and has no pre-batch contributor. B would split the two askers' meaning.
  - *Conditions.* The seat should confirm A explicitly before landing, and M4 should declare what A leaves refused.
- Split-out (the PR's acceptance note): uninstalling, disabling or enabling a supplier extension does not ask the door. The ruling allows "pin, or file separately", so the seat should file the card.
- CI is not part of this verdict. At `fb22e7bd` the required checks were still in progress when I read them.

### ④ Design judgment

**The design is right.**
- Judging the served fold instead of the bare body removes a whole exemption class, instead of patching one more case.
- Comparing against "before" puts the blame on the change, which matches R6's reason.
- `servedFoldWithLayer` reuses `foldExtenders` and `withholdDisabledExtensions`, so the door and the served read cannot drift apart.

**The faults are in three places, and each fix is local:**
- the identity key (M2),
- one unpinned arm (M3),
- two declarations that say less (M1) or more (M4) than the code does.

**Nits:**
- **N1:** the body's `priority` is dropped. Both `protocol-save.ts:1269` and `batch-object-registration.ts:167` discard it, so the fold sorts the incoming extension at `followDoorSlotPriority` (`registry.ts:5926`), not at the priority the write-through will register (`registerObjectExtension`). This matters only when two extensions add the same field. Pass `priority` through `FollowDoorLayer`, or say why it is ignored.
- **N2:** nothing pins the overlay arm's `replaced` capture (`registry.ts:6193`). One reload pin with an environment overlay over a cold-boot-admitted pair would cover it.
- **N3:** `protocol-save.ts:1263` declares an inline structural type for `objectRegistrationRefusal`. `batch-object-registration.ts` already has `JudgingRegistry` with the same signature, so one shared type would keep the two in step.
- **N4:** `e61155be` handles the stale sentence in `18.record-currency-follow-pair-refused-on-install-and-reload.ts:46-47` by superseding it from the new entry, and leaves the registered entry unedited. That is acceptable. The seat decides whether to amend the registered entry instead.

Implemented-by: `claude/area-E2b-33593`
Reviewed-by: `session_016WV4d1PGptBW3QRQNmy5e6`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

domain:server#5 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4cz4f7zEQZ2C9GTG382
Request: delta review · area E2b · head f1f49b35 · Fixes #33593 (after FAIL 6888559585 on fb22e7bd)

- M1: declared. The published `object_extension` single save asks D6's roll-up door as well as the follow door, as the batch writer's extension row already did. FROM stored 200 + warn TO refused 422 INVALID_METADATA, nothing stored. This is in the changeset, the semantic entry, the registry-question.ts header and the body table. Pinned (sum roll-up over `ledger_own_line.amount`).
- M2: R7 now compares the refused pair (`followPairKey`: kind, object, field, target), not the message. Pinned: a parent upgrade that only adds an unrelated code field installs.
- M3: pinned the extension package's own no-change upgrade, which installs. In an ablation of the extend-arm capture, only this pin went red.
- M4: the changeset scopes R7 to runs (seat 5: A). It adds that an unchanged extension re-published via single save or the batch writer moves FROM saved TO refused 422.
- The new entry supersedes, for runs, semantic/18's "although nothing in that package is wrong"; the registered entry is untouched. Follow-up for uninstall/disable/enable: #33628.
- Local runs at f1f49b35: objectql 595 files / 13099 tests, touched files 65/65, adr-0087-registration and spec-changes exit 0, eslint exit 0. main (#33513) merged clean. Not run locally: the dogfood battery and objectql dependents (owed before arming); N1–N3 not addressed.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f1f49b3514dee2f5365c621673e4208ad81d0421`
Local-runs: none
Scope: `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.record-currency-follow-extension-judged-as-served.ts` + `.changeset/33593-extension-follow-judged-as-served.md`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save.ts`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/registry-question.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/record-currency-aggregate-door.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/manifest-service-artifact-refusal-restores.test.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/protocol-batch-object-registration.test.ts`

Delta review after the FAIL at `fb22e7bd` (comment 6888559585), against the area's request (comment 6888771065). Read: the two new commits `89d28000` and `f1f49b35` (`git diff fb22e7bd f1f49b35`, 6 files, +72/−19), the full PR diff where a finding needed it, the PR body at this head, and main's door at `c32bb6cc` for FROM readings. The head has not moved past `f1f49b35`. Line numbers are at `f1f49b35`. I ran no test, build or gate. Every behaviour below is by reading.

### ① Derived judgments

**Round-1 must-fixes.**

- **M1 (round 1) — closed in the code and the pin; the declaration is short by one arm (see new M1 below).** The `protocol-save.ts` hunk (`:1257-1273`) is unchanged and still asks D6's roll-up door through `objectRegistrationRefusal(..., 'extend', { againstRegistry: true })` (`registry.ts:5820`). It is now declared in the changeset (`:26`), the PR table, the entry's `surface`, and `registry-question.ts:16-18`. The pin `protocol-batch-object-registration.test.ts:528` saves an `object_extension` adding `sum(ledger_own_line.amount)` over an own-currency amount and asserts 422 `INVALID_METADATA`, no registered field and no active row. I checked the emitter: `RecordCurrencySummaryRefusedError` carries `code = RECORD_CURRENCY_SUMMARY_REFUSED_CODE = 'INVALID_METADATA'` and `status = 422` (`record-currency-aggregate-door.ts:224`, `:232-235`), so the sentence's code is right. Without the hunk the save stores the row and that pin goes red.
- **M2 (round 1) — the sentence is no longer compared, but the pair key leaves out the parent the pair points at (see new M2 below).** `recordCurrencyFollowRefusal` now compares `followPairKey(kind, object, field, target)` (`record-currency-aggregate-door.ts:536-557`). The round-1 example (a parent upgrade that only adds `cc`) is pinned (`manifest-service-artifact-refusal-restores.test.ts:950`): the old message key would refuse it, the new key installs it.
- **M3 (round 1) — closed.** `manifest-service-artifact-refusal-restores.test.ts:941` boots with the bad extension, upgrades `extender` unchanged to 1.0.1, and asserts it installs and still serves `invoice.title`. By reading, dropping the extend arm's `replaced` capture makes `before` the empty slot, which holds no `ext_amount`, so this pin goes red. That matches the area's ablation claim.
- **M4 (round 1) — closed.** The changeset now scopes the R7 line to runs (`:24`, matching seat 5's ruling A) and adds the unchanged-extension re-publish line for single save and the batch writer (`:25`). The entry's `reason` says the same.

**must-fix M1: the D6 line describes only one of the two roll-ups D6 refuses, and the entry leaves out the other direction.**

- *What D6 refuses.* `recordCurrencySummaryRefusal` refuses `sum` / `avg` / `min` / `max` of any child amount `recordCurrencyAggregandOf` returns a code for, which is every `currencyMode: 'record'` amount. `rollupVerdict` (`record-currency-aggregate-door.ts:334-350`) admits only one shape: the amount follows that very parent's code through the very master_detail the roll-up reads. So it also refuses a roll-up of a *following* amount that is read on another parent, or through another relation (the `follows` arm of the error, `:259-270`).
- *What the texts say.* The changeset (`:26`), the PR table's last row, and the entry's `surface` all say "a child amount whose rows carry their own currency". That covers the own-code arm only. An `object_extension` single save that adds a `sum` of a following amount through the wrong relation also moves FROM stored 200 (registration warned) TO refused 422, and nothing declares it.
- *The entry is shorter still.* The changeset also lists "an amount a registered parent's such roll-up reads" (D6's second loop, `:379-398`). The entry's `surface` names only the roll-up the extension adds.
- *Fix (text only, no new pin needed, since the existing pin proves the door is asked):* in the changeset `:26`, the PR table row and the entry's `surface`, say "a child amount declared `currencyMode: 'record'` (in each row's own currency, or following a parent's code but not read on that parent through the master_detail it follows)". Add D6's second direction to the entry's `surface`.

**must-fix M2: the R7 pair key does not include the object the amount follows, so a run that re-points the pair onto another bad parent is admitted, and that answer moves undeclared.**
